{{Quote|Every so-called Jedi on Tython is going to die. That's a promise. Your entire order is weak. You've done nothing to stop the Sith Empire's advances.|Bengel Morr|<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" />}}
Near the end of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], the native [[Flesh Raider]]s of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tython/Legends|Tython]] began to '''wage war''' against the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and the [[Pilgrims]] of [[Kalikori village|Kalikori Village]]. Under the command of the [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Bengel Morr]], the Flesh Raiders became more bold in their attacks against the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], who had returned to their Order's ancestral [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] in the aftermath of the [[Sacking of Coruscant]] and the end of the [[Great Galactic War]]. Morr, who had been driven insane by the devastation during the fall of the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], blamed the Jedi Order for the defeat and turned to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], taking on the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Callef]] as his apprentice and plotting the destruction of the Order.

In [[3643 BBY]], Morr set his plans in motion by [[Attack on the Gnarls Outpost|sending]] Callef and a Flesh Raider invasion force against the [[Gnarls Outpost|Jedi outpost]] in the [[Tythonian Gnarls]] region. However, Callef was [[Duel in the Gnarls cave|defeated]] and [[Death/Legends|killed]] by a [[Hero of Tython|young Jedi initiate]], who was then taken on as an [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]] by the Human [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]], Morr's former teacher. Together with Din and the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[T7-O1]], the apprentice learned of Morr's survival and vendetta against the Order during the course of several missions for both the Jedi and the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] settlers of Kalikori. Upon discovering that Morr had organized the natives into an [[Army/Legends|army]] and was training some of them as [[Force Adept]]s, the Jedi [[Raid on the Tythos Ridge shield generator|moved]] to [[Assault on the Flesh Raider command base|eliminate]] the [[Flesh Raider command base]] and several [[Raid on the Forsaken Den|other]] camps in an attempt to put a stop to Morr's planned assault on the Order.

However, Din and his apprentice were betrayed by the villagers when Morr made a deal with the Twi'leks, trading protection from the Flesh Raiders in exchange for the life of his former Master and Din's new Padawan. While Morr took his unconscious mentor to the ancient machine known as the [[Vur Tepe|Forge]], the villagers attempted to kill Din's apprentice and T7-O1 as part of an altered deal, but the Padawan managed to escape without [[Blood/Legends|bloodshed]] and pursued Morr through the Tythan wilderness. Fighting through the Flesh Raider army occupying the ruins of an [[Ruined Tythonian city|ancient city]], the Padawan and T7-O1 found Morr waiting before the Forge. In a [[Battle of the Forge|fierce duel]], the young apprentice defeated the deranged Morr and rescued Din from his former student. For the Padawan's bravery and actions, Din ordered his apprentice to construct a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and return to the [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Jedi Temple]], where Morr was healed of his insanity and the apprentice elevated to the rank of [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]]. Along with T7-O1, the Knight's first assignment soon spiraled into war as the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Angral]] launched a [[Desolator crisis|campaign]] against the Republic, and the young Jedi played a pivotal role in the conflict by ultimately defeating the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] in a [[Battle of the Oppressor|battle]] above Tython.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|The temple was annihilated. Hundreds of Jedi died that day. We never recovered all the bodies. Bengel was strong in the Force, and the most gentle being I've ever known. For him to turn against the Jedi&hellip; he has to be stopped.|Orgus Din, on the Sacking of Coruscant and Bengel Morr|<ref name="Enemy Force" />}}
The origins of the [[Flesh Raider]]s' uprising could be traced back to the [[Great Galactic War]], a lengthy conflict between the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]] and the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. The war's end occurred in [[3653 BBY]], when the Empire used sham [[Alderaan peace conference|peace negotiations]] on the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core World]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] to stage an attack on the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], a battle that would become known as the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]. In order to force the Republic to submit and to bring an end to the conflict between the two [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] powers, the Empire held the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] captive while the [[Treaty of Coruscant]] was signed on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="Timeline 1">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant|int=Timeline 1: Treaty of Coruscant}}</ref> As the first part of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] assault, a strike team decimated the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]], [[Death/Legends|killing]] the building's defenders and finally destroying it with explosives.<ref name="SW:TOR:Deceived">''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''</ref>

[[File:Bengel_Morr_Holo.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Bengel Morr]]
[[Bengel Morr]], the [[Nautolan/Legends|Nautolan]] [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]] of the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Orgus Din]], was present in the Temple during the assault, but he fled into the ruins of the structure when the Sith collapsed the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order's]] headquarters. His gentle personality shattered, the Nautolan retreated into the depths of the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|city-planet]] and was assumed dead by his comrades when his body was not recovered. Morr blamed the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Order for the destruction of the Temple, believing that their weakness had allowed the Sith to win the war. He decided that for the Sith to be defeated, the Order had to be destroyed and rebuilt from its ashes. Turning to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] and becoming a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]], Morr spent the next [[Time/Legends|decade]] plotting the destruction of the Order.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> During this time, he recruited the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Human [[Callef]] as his apprentice, training the young man in the ways of the dark side.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />

===Resettling on Tython===
{{Quote|There's a group of Pilgrims on Tython. They've been fighting the Flesh Raiders for months. The Republic wanted us to deny those Twi'leks aid&mdash;they settled here illegally&mdash;but frankly, we need them.|Orgus Din|<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />}}
After the signing of the Treaty, the devastation of Coruscant and the Empire's victory turned public opinion against the Jedi, and the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]]&mdash;looking for someone to blame for the disaster&mdash;decided to delay the reconstruction of the Jedi Temple indefinitely. Realizing that the capital was no longer the best place for its headquarters, the Order relocated to its ancestral [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Tython/Legends|Tython]],<ref name="Timeline 1" /> which had been discovered only a [[3651 BBY|year earlier]] by a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] named [[Satele Shan]]. There, they established a new [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Jedi Temple]] and began to explore the ancient ruins left by their precursors,<ref name="Codex Temple">{{TORcite|type=codex|Jedi Temple (Tython)}}</ref> the [[Je'daii Order]].<ref name="DotJ">[[Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi 0|''Star Wars: Dawn of the Jedi'' 0]]</ref> Construction on the new Temple began about [[3650 BBY/Legends|three years]] after the fall of the Temple on Coruscant, just over a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] since the Order had rediscovered Tython and established a permanent settlement on the planet, and it took almost [[3647 BBY|three years]] to complete.<ref name="Codex Temple" />

Throughout the next decade or so, the Jedi recovered from the devastating losses that they incurred during the war and slowly rebuilt their ranks. Not long after the Order arrived on the planet, a group of [[Pilgrims]] petitioned the Senate for permission to settle on Tython, as they had fled religious persecution on their homeworld of [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]]. However, as Tython was still largely unexplored, the Senate refused their request. In direct defiance of the decree, the Pilgrims established a small settlement in a valley above the Jedi Temple, just on the edge of the [[Tythos Ridge]] mountain range. That camp grew into the settlement of [[Kalikori village|Kalikori Village]], with a villager named [[Sumari]] in the role of [[Matriarch/Legends|Matriarch]] by the time of the war with the Flesh Raiders.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

[[File:Kalikori_village.png|thumb|right|200px|Kalikori Village suffered greatly from Flesh Raider attacks during the Cold War.]]
By [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Time" /> Callef and Morr followed the Order to Tython. There, hiding from the Order in the widely unexplored regions of the planet, the two Dark Jedi began to marshal the Flesh Raiders, Tython's native [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], into an [[Army/Legends|army]].<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" /> Finding some of the violent species to be [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-sensitive, Morr trained them to be [[Force Adept]]s<ref name="Enemy Force" /> and eventually commanded a significant fighting force<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> under the leadership of the Flesh Raiders' [[Grand Chieftain]] [[Keshk]].<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> Before Morr's arrival, the natives had been largely unorganized, but they had launched periodic raids upon both the Jedi and Kalikori Village throughout the last decade with varying amounts of success.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

The Force-wielding Jedi Order easily repelled the natives' attacks, losing only young and inexperienced Jedi to groups of Flesh Raiders,<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" /> but the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] villagers fared far worse. Largely unprepared for the attacks and outmatched by the natives' ferocity, Kalikori suffered heavy losses throughout their time on the planet, and the Jedi Order's adherence to the Senate's request to refuse them aid fostered intense resentment of the Jedi in the people of Kalikori. Matters only worsened for the villagers when the Flesh Raiders became more organized under Morr's leadership, and the natives began to attack more frequently and in greater numbers.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

===Early encounters===
{{GameLSmechanics|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
{{Quote|Flesh Raider attacks are up. Three in the past day. Just last night they dragged a dozen Pilgrims into the darkness.|Master Meeb Wix|<ref name="Flesh Raider Factfinding">{{TORcite|type=general|Flesh Raider Factfinding|Tython}}</ref>}}
One of the Flesh Raider attacks killed a village patrol, including a Twi'lek named [[Poronth Ghon]], and Poronth's son [[Tazonthe Ghon|Tazonthe]] enlisted the aid of a Jedi to find his [[Parent/Legends|father]]. The Jedi discovered the elder Ghon's remains and returned his [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] to Tazonthe, but the man was furious that the Jedi refused to slaughter the Flesh Raiders in revenge.<ref name="Lost Pilgrim">{{TORcite|type=general|Lost Pilgrim|Tython}}</ref> The villager [[Bahlea]] was aided by a member of the Order when a Jedi retrieved [[Manka cat/Legends|manka cat]] [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] for a medical remedy, completing her fallen husband's mission and saving her daughter [[Rusa]]. [[Vederiat Ayon]], one of the village's healers, learned from a injured village warrior that the Flesh Raiders were experimenting with elixirs and had succeeding in creating one that drove the natives into a primal fury. She asked a visiting Jedi to destroy the elixir, and sent the Jedi to the guard [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Odumis Mer]] in order to learn the location of the elixir vats. Mer asked the Jedi to bring the elixir back so that the villagers could use it, but they refused and traveled into the Tythos Ridge to destroy the elixir before informing Ayon of Mer's request. The healer realized that the Captain's mind had been addled by encounters with the natives, so she relieved him of duty so that he could be healed<ref name="Strength of the Flesh Raiders">{{TORcite|type=general|Strength of the Flesh Raiders|Tython}}</ref> and appointed [[Bashenn]] in his place.<ref name="Pilgrims" />

[[File:Fashk.png|thumb|left|140px|Fashk was allowed to join the Jedi Order, despite his species' violent tendencies.]]
The Jedi Order's encounters with the natives often had more success than those of the Twi'leks, such as the repeated attempts to destroy the [[Gnarls Outpost|Jedi outpost]] in the [[Tythonian Gnarls]] region.<ref name="Path of a Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Path of a Jedi|Tython}}</ref> A group of Padawans&mdash;[[Avitla]], [[Mennaus]], and [[Jerridan]]&mdash;were ambushed by Flesh Raiders in the Gnarls, injuring Jerridan and worrying Master [[Relnex]] when they did not return. The Padawans were rescued by another Jedi,<ref name="Early Lessons">{{TORcite|type=general|Early Lessons|Tython}}</ref> though Flesh Raiders continued to stage attacks and kidnap inexperienced apprentices, imprisoning them in cages throughout the Gnarls.<ref name="Captured Padawans">{{TORcite|type=general|Captured Padawans|Tython}}</ref> Another Jedi discovered a Flesh Raider [[Youngling/Legends|infant]] in the mountains near the Temple, and delivered the child to Master [[Quilb]], who often took in orphaned animals.<ref name="Flesh Eating Baby">{{TORcite|type=general|Flesh Eating Baby|Tython}}</ref>

Through the efforts of various members of the Order, the Jedi gained insight into the natives' culture<ref name="Flesh Raider Factfinding" /> and even recruited the Flesh Raider [[Fashk]] into the Order itself.<ref name="New Recruit">{{TORcite|type=general|New Recruit|Tython}}</ref> Masters [[Kalisa Gehnso]] and [[Meeb Wix]] enlisted the aid of another Jedi to investigate the Flesh Raiders' religious idols&mdash;the [[Bone Idol]], [[Flesh Idol]], and [[Salvage Idol]]&mdash;in an attempt to learn what inspired the natives' aggressive behavior,<ref name="Flesh Raider Factfinding" /> and the Twi'lek villager [[Trea Kobbeth]] asked a Jedi to rescue her son [[Viyo Kobbeth|Viyo]] from the Tythos Ridge. The Jedi discovered that Viyo had been captured by Fashk to serve as a translator, and that the Force-sensitive Flesh Raider wished to be [[Jedi training/Legends|trained]] as a Jedi. Fashk's surprising request was approved by Master [[Strayen]], the Master in charge of administrating the new recruits on Tython, and Viyo was released by the Flesh Raider before Fashk traveled to the Jedi Temple to be trained. Strayen hoped to temper Fashk's violent nature and show him the ways of the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]], since without Jedi training the Flesh Raider would likely succumb to the dark side.<ref name="New Recruit" />

===Tensions rise===
{{Main|Search for the Fount of Rajivari}}
During the [[Standard month/Legends|months]] leading up to Morr's assault, a [[Search for the Fount of Rajivari|minor conflict]] broke out over the mystical [[Fount of Rajivari]], a lost repository of knowledge left by the ancient Jedi. One of the Twi'lek villagers, a Force-sensitive named [[Nalen Raloch]], was seduced to the dark side by the teachings of [[Rajivari]], one of the first fallen Jedi who had played a major role in the [[Force Wars]] of ancient times. Furious that the Order refused to help his people against the Flesh Raiders,<ref name="Pilgrims" /> Raloch uncovered the Fount&mdash;which was in fact Rajivari's own [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]]<ref name="Rajivari's Legacy">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|Rajivari's Legacy|Tython}}</ref>&mdash;and, with his new powers, attempted to destroy the ancient machine known as the [[Vur Tepe|Forge]]. The Forge was a device built by the Je'daii to construct [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], and the Jedi Order had continued to send their Padawans there upon as part of the [[Jedi Trials/Legends|Jedi Trials]] upon their return to Tython.<ref name="Forge Codex">{{TORcite|type=codex|The Forge}}</ref> Raloch was stopped, however, by the [[The Barsen'thor|apprentice]] of Jedi Master [[Yuon Par]] in a [[Duel at the Forge|duel]], and was successfully cured of his insanity. Raloch would be trained as a Jedi by the Order in an attempt to improve relations with Kalikori,<ref name="The Forge">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Consular|The Forge|Tython}}</ref> but the village still harbored intense resentment because of the Order's continued refusal of aid.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />
{{Endgame}}

==The uprising==
{{GameLSmechanics|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
===A dark encounter===
{{Quote|&laquo;He commands the Flesh Raiders attacking us.&raquo;<br />''"''Not attacking&mdash;cleansing. And we have only begun.|quotestart=0|Unaw Aharo and Callef|<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />}}
[[File:Callef_and_Aharo.png|thumb|right|200px|The encounter with Callef revealed that there was more to the invasion than the Jedi thought.]]
In 3643 BBY,<ref name="Time" /> the Flesh Raiders captured [[T7-O1]], one of twenty reconnaissance [[Droid/Legends|droids]] sent out by the Jedi Order, and placed the droid with a [[Restraining bolt/Legends|restraining bolt]] in the [[Upper Hollows]] cave system in the Tythos Ridge. Around this time, Bengel Morr decided to put his plans in action&mdash;meeting with Callef in the Upper Hollows, he ordered his apprentice to take a detachment of Flesh Raiders and invade the Gnarls through a [[Gnarls cave|recently discovered cave]] connecting the region to the Tythos Ridge. T7-O1 witnessed the meeting and secretly made a recording of it, as the Flesh Raiders did not know that the droid was still active.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

By that point, Morr's army had established a great number of small camps across much of Tython,<ref name="Dark Temptations">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Dark Temptations|Tython}}</ref> and he had begun to send Force-sensitive Flesh Raiders to study the Force from [[Holocron/Legends|holocrons]] amidst the ancient ruins that dotted the planet.<ref name="Enemy Force" /> The natives' [[Flesh Raider command base|main command base]] was located high in the Tythos Ridge, protected by a [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] on a nearby mountain, and from there Morr's subordinates coordinated the Flesh Raider army.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> One of the smaller bases was located in the cave network known as the [[Forsaken Den]], in the cliffs near the ruins of [[Kaleth]], and Flesh Raiders had been learning from a holocron at a [[Ancient shrine|nearby shrine]].<ref name="Enemy Force" /> An ancient temple-[[City/Legends|city]] of the Jedi's predecessors, the Je'daii Order,<ref name="DotJ" /> Kaleth had been the site of several battles during the devastating Force Wars, and the Jedi Order had been cautiously investigating the outer ruins since their return<ref name="Codex Kaleth">{{TORcite|type=codex|Kaleth}}</ref>&mdash;making it a perfect place for Flesh Raiders to pass relatively unnoticed.<ref name="Enemy Force" />

Just as Callef led his forces through the tunnel and into the Gnarls, a young [[Hero of Tython|Jedi initiate]] arrived on Tython to take the Jedi Trials. The apprentice departed aboard a [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] arriving at the [[Masters' Retreat]], a meditation enclave north of the Jedi Temple, and met with Jedi Master [[Derrin Weller]]. Weller planned to send the young Jedi to the Temple to meet with the Masters, but at that moment Callef's forces reached the Gnarls Outpost and began to [[Attack on the Gnarls Outpost|attack]] the Jedi there. A [[Bith/Legends|Bith]] apprentice by the name of [[Unaw Aharo]] witnessed the Flesh Raiders coming through the cave, but by the time he contacted Weller via [[Holocomm/Legends|holocomm]], the Flesh Raiders were already at the Jedi outpost.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />

Alarmed, Weller immediately ordered the Knights present at the Masters' Retreat across the [[Water/Legends|lake]] separating the structure from the Gnarls, where they mounted a defense of the Gnarls Outpost against the natives. As the base was relatively undermanned, Weller sent the newly arrived apprentice into the Gnarls, since the learner was remarkably skilled in combat. During the course of the fight, Weller was injured, and he contacted the apprentice before taking a shuttle back to the Temple [[Medcenter/Legends|medcenter]]. Weller needed the apprentice, who was already deep in the Gnarls, to seal off the cave through which the Flesh Raiders were coming, since the other Jedi in the area were all needed to defend the outpost.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />

[[File:Bringing_down_the_house.png|thumb|left|180px|Orgus Din seals the tunnel to the Gnarls.]]
A group of Flesh Raiders had discovered Aharo not long after the Bith had contacted Weller, and the natives injured the apprentice before capturing him and taking him into the caves to Callef. The Dark Jedi began to interrogate Aharo, while the other apprentice located the cave and fought a path through the Flesh Raiders within. The initiate arrived just as Callef was preparing to execute his [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]], and the young Jedi's attempt to stop Callef sparked a [[Duel in the Gnarls cave|duel]] between the two. Despite the Dark Jedi's experience and use of a lightsaber, Callef was [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|defeated]] and killed in the fight.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />

On his way to the Jedi Temple, Weller had called ahead and informed the other Masters of the battle in the Gnarls, and Orgus Din was dispatched to aid the apprentice in sealing the cave. Din arrived just as the initiate struck down Callef, and he was relieved to learn that both the apprentice and Aharo were still alive. Astonished that Callef had wielded a lightsaber&mdash;one that was strangely familiar to him&mdash;Din sealed off the cavern by collapsing the tunnel with the Force. While Din escorted the wounded Aharo back to a medcenter, Din ordered the other apprentice to travel to the Jedi Temple.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />

===Early missions===
{{Quote|My scouts have tracked the Flesh Raiders for months. Watched them grow in strength. I will share what we've discovered, but only if you agree to protect my people. We&hellip; we suffer&hellip;|Matriarch Sumari|<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />}}
At the Temple, Din surprised the rest of the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] by taking on the young apprentice as a Padawan&mdash;his first since Bengel Morr's disappearance a decade earlier. Believing that the Force had brought the two together, Din assigned his new student a first mission: establish contact with the Pilgrims in Kalikori Village and learn what they knew about the Flesh Raider attacks. However, Matriarch Sumari was displeased that the Jedi were only reaching out when their own safety was threatened, and only agreed to share her information if the apprentice would help protect the village. As she had recently fallen ill, Sumari was forced to retire early, but the Padawan continued to speak with Sumari's daughter [[Ranna Tao'Ven]] and the village's [[Scout Chief]] [[Moorint]]. In return for information on the Flesh Raiders' activities, the two Twi'leks asked the young Jedi to steal a weapons cache from a group of Flesh Raiders nearby.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

Venturing into the mountains of the Tythos Ridge, the apprentice [[Raid on the Flesh Raider weapons cache|fought]] through the Flesh Raider&ndash;infested region and entered the camp in the Upper Hollows cave system. After defeating [[Unidentified Flesh Raider Warmaster|one]] of the natives' [[Warmaster (Flesh Raider)|Warmasters]], the Padawan used the Flesh Raider's key to access the cache and recover the weapons. During the apprentice's raid, a group of Flesh Raiders made an [[Attack on Kalikori village|attack]] on Kalikori, killing several villagers before they were driven back. However, there were more than just weapons and supplies in the chamber&mdash;the cache was the same one that the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] T7-O1 was being held in, and the droid immediately recognized the young apprentice as a Jedi. Upon the removal of the bolt, T7-O1 showed the Padawan his recording of Morr giving orders to Callef, though the apprentice only recognized Callef and not the hooded figure he called "Master."<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

Returning to Kalikori with the weapons and T7-O1, the young Jedi delivered the [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] and supplies to the villagers and learned of the Flesh Raider attack when a villager named [[Saylew]] angrily confronted Tao'ven and Moorint. The pair met with Din, who had arrived [[Standard minute/Legends|minutes]] earlier, and showed him the recording.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> Din recognized the voice as that of Morr,<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> although he did not tell his student, and ordered the apprentice to speak with Moorint while he viewed the recording again. Fulfilling the deal, Moorint and Tao'Ven shared their information: the Flesh Raiders had been gathering in strength for several months, and several of the natives had recently been spotted near the ruins of Kaleth.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" />

While Din returned to the Temple to discuss the recording with the other Masters, the apprentice traveled to the ruins of Kaleth and explored the ancient shrine where the Flesh Raiders had been sighted. It was not long before Moorint's reports were confirmed&mdash;the Flesh Raiders were in fact using the shrine as a base, while some of the natives studied from a holocron<ref name="Enemy Force" /> given to them by Morr.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> The Padawan was alarmed to learn that some of the Flesh Raiders were Force-sensitive, and after [[Skirmish at the ancient shrine|defeating]] the group's [[Flesh Raider Ravager Chieftain|leader]], recovered a holocron from their corpses. Showing the holocron to Master [[Bela Kiwiiks]] and her Padawan [[Kira Carsen]], who had been sent as reinforcements just before they departed for Coruscant, the apprentice was instructed to set up security devices in the area to track activity.<ref name="Enemy Force" />

===War in earnest===
{{Quote|Why spread our forces thin to hit all the camps at once?''"<br />"''If we only go after a few, the Flesh Raiders could warn the rest and regroup.|The Padawan and Orgus Din|<ref name="Dark Temptations" />}}
[[File:Tythos_Ridge_High.png|thumb|right|180px|The Tythos Ridge had a heavy Flesh Raider presence during the uprising.]]
During the apprentice's mission, Sumari succumbed to her illness, leaving her daughter Tao'Ven as the new Matriarch. Upon returning to Kalikori Village, the apprentice met with Din and Tao'Ven in the Matriarch's compound, and Din decided to reveal what he had been holding back earlier: the identity of the hooded figure from the recording. Explaining Morr's background, Din urged his apprentice not to engage him if encountered on the next mission&mdash;the Dark Jedi was likely extremely dangerous. Tao'Ven and Moorint then shared that scouts had located the natives' command base in the nearby mountains, but it was protected by a [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]]. While Din and the other Masters prepared to [[Assault on the Flesh Raider command base|raid the camp]], Din's apprentice [[Raid on the Tythos Ridge shield generator|attacked]] the mountain where the shield generator was set up.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" />

Storming the mountain cavern, the Padawan fought through the Flesh Raiders guarding the generator and successfully deactivated it. At the same time, a group of Flesh Raiders attacked Kalikori, breaking through the village's defenses and planting [[toxin mine]]s in the settlement's agricultural fields as part of a scorched-earth tactic. Once the shield was down, however, Morr contacted the Padawan via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] and expressed his displeasure, swearing to destroy the Jedi Order and warning the apprentice that the Jedi's efforts were futile. Worried about Morr's threats, the Padawan returned to Kalikori to alert the Masters, but the apprentice found the village in a state of war. The villagers were unable to eliminate the Flesh Raider [[Saboteur/Legends|saboteurs]] in their fields, but the Padawan successfully braved the toxic gas and [[Skirmish in the Kalikori village fields|defeated]] the natives before too much damage could be done. By risking one's life and successfully disabling the mines, the Jedi trainee earned the personal loyalty of Tao'Ven,<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> something that would have powerful repercussions in later events.<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

[[File:Kaleth_Duel.png|thumb|left|180px|The Padawan successfully destroyed the base in the Forsaken Den, despite the native resistance.]]
Not long after the Masters departed for their raid, a [[Selkath/Legends|Selkath]] Jedi Knight named [[Laotah]] detected Flesh Raider activity near Kaleth<ref name="Dark Temptations" /> on the scanners that had been set up by the apprentice,<ref name="Enemy Force" /> and he chose to investigate on his own. However, Laotah was unprepared to combat the Force-sensitive natives within the Forsaken Den, and he was quickly overpowered and fatally wounded. As Laotah crawled back to the cave's entrance, [[Flesh Raider Bladewielder|one]] of the Flesh Raiders stole the injured Jedi's lightsaber and took it as his own.<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

During their raid on the Flesh Raider command base, the Masters discovered the locations of the other Flesh Raider camps across the planet, and upon their return they began to organize the Knights at the Temple to eliminate the encampments. Din returned to Kalikori to send his apprentice on another mission, as the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Council]] was allowing Din's student to destroy one of the camps alone on account of the Padawan's experience and skill. As the Flesh Raider force that the apprentice had fought earlier had been based at the Forsaken Den near Kaleth, Din decided to send his student to destroy that base.<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

While Din himself struck at a camp in the nearby mountains, the Padawan fought through a number of ancient [[Tythonian War Droid|war droids]]&mdash;machines left over from the Force Wars that still guarded the ruins of Kaleth and attacked any who ventured into the city&mdash;and entered the Forsaken Den to find the mortally injured Laotah. Learning what had happened to the Selkath and promising to recover Laotah's lightsaber, the Padawan stayed with the other Jedi until his death and then [[Raid on the Forsaken Den|raided]] the compound within, defeating the Force-wielding natives and fighting the blade-wielding Flesh Raider to the death.<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

===Endgame===
{{Quote|You're stronger than any Jedi I've known. You could redeem the order and destroy the Sith. I understand. You are the weapon I came to forge.|Bengel Morr, after his defeat|<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />}}
While the Jedi struck at Flesh Raider camps across the planet, Morr had a new goal: capturing his former Master. To that end, he took advantage of the Order's preoccupation with his Flesh Raider army and approached Kalikori mere minutes after Din and his student departed. The Dark Jedi met with Moorint and several other villagers, purposely excluding Matriarch Tao'Ven, and offered them a deal: give up Din, and their village would be spared from any further attack by Flesh Raiders. Seeing a way to save themselves and to get even with the Jedi for refusing them aid, the settlers agreed and informed Tao'Ven. While she did not like the plan, she went along with it on one condition: the life of Din's apprentice would be spared. Morr agreed, and the villagers broadcast a fake [[Distress signal/Legends|distress call]] from the village.<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

When the apprentice contacted Din to report success, the Jedi Master ordered his apprentice to respond to the distress call and rendezvous with him at the village. Din and his apprentice were the only ones close enough to reach the village in time, as the rest of the Jedi were scattered across the planet, and the two raced back to the settlement. Yet when Din arrived at the village first, the Nautolan's Flesh Raider [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] knocked the Jedi Master unconscious. Departing Kalikori, Morr briefly mentioned to Tao'Ven that his destination was somewhere called "the Forge."<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

Not long after Morr left, the Padawan arrived and immediately questioned Tao'Ven as to the reason for the distress signal. Tao'Ven lied, saying that she didn't know anything about a signal, and that she had not seen the apprentice's Master. T7-O1, who had returned to the village after a brief scouting mission, could not detect Din in the village. However, at that moment Morr was contacting the villagers and changing his deal: he would only protect the village if they killed Morr's apprentice. Worried about their safety, several villagers rushed into the Matriarch's building just as the Padawan turned to question the Matriarch further, and they knocked out the Jedi from behind before hitting T7-O1 with an [[Ion blaster/Legends|ion blast]].<ref name="Dark Temptations" />

After delivering the message to the villagers, Morr and his Flesh Raider servants continued their journey through the Flesh Raider&ndash;controlled Tythos Ridge<ref name="Dark Temptations" /> toward the ruins of an [[Ruined Tythonian city|ancient city]]. The ruins was under the control of the Flesh Raider army, led by Grand Chieftain Keshk, and Morr ordered his subordinate to mobilize his forces in the ruins in preparation for their assault on the Jedi Order.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

[[File:Morr_and_Din.png|thumb|right|190px|Morr believed his former master was weak for submitting to the Treaty of Coruscant.]]
When several of the villagers&mdash;Moorint, [[Eseni]], and Saylew&mdash;attempted to kill the unconscious apprentice, Tao'Ven intervened and begged them to stop. The Padawan awoke quickly and learned the truth of the villagers' betrayal, but before the situation could escalate into [[Blood/Legends|bloodshed]] the Jedi [[Mind trick/Legends|persuaded]] the villagers to leave in peace. Begging for forgiveness, the Matriarch told the apprentice that Morr was heading to the Forge, and allowed the Padawan to leave with T7-O1.<ref name="Dark Temptations" /> The duo immediately contacted [[A-4P0]], one of the droids at the [[Jedi Archives (Tython)|Temple Archives]], and ordered the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] to send all of the information on the Forge to T7-O1.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

Complying with the request, A-4P0 warned that all of the Jedi Masters were still occupied fighting the Flesh Raiders, and those Jedi thus would be unable to assist them. Using a different path to reach the Forge than Morr, the pair raced along the [[Elarian Trail]] and used a tunnel behind the [[Tythos River]]'s [[Forbidden Falls|waterfall]] to reach the ruins of the ancient city. Some of Morr's Flesh Raider [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] had learned to reprogram the ancient [[Battle droid/Legends|war droids]] that littered the area, and the droids were incorporated into their army. Despite the heavy presence of Flesh Raiders and war droids in their path, T7-O1 and the Padawan successfully fought their way through the ruins and reached the caverns beyond.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

Emerging in the canyon where the Forge stood, the Padawan and T7-O1 fought through over a dozen of Morr's Flesh Raider Force Adepts and crossed the rocky bridge to the ancient machine. There, before the Forge, the pair faced Morr and his two bodyguards next to the unconscious body of Din. Drawing his [[Color/Legends|yellow]] lightsaber, Morr [[Battle of the Forge|attacked]] the young Jedi and T7-O1 with his bodyguards. With the aid of T7-O1, the Padawan successfully defeated the Flesh Raiders and began to duel the Dark Jedi.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

Despite his advantages of a lightsaber and greater experience, Morr&mdash;like his apprentice Callef before him&mdash;was unable to defeat the Jedi and lost the duel, his weapon knocked aside. Believing that the Force had guided him to his own defeat for a reason, Morr offered to share his knowledge of the dark side and prepare the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] for the apprentice's coming. Understanding now that the young Jedi before him was the weapon he had come to forge, the Nautolan expressed his belief that the Padawan was strong enough to destroy the Sith.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

The younger apprentice refused, however, and punched Morr in the gut when the latter reached for his blade. A second strike to the back of Morr's neck sent him to the ground unconscious, and Din's apprentice turned to wake his Master. Praising his student on the successful battle and the decision to spare Morr's life, Din gave his apprentice the components necessary to build a lightsaber and instructed the Jedi to use the Forge to craft the weapon. While Din took his former student back to the Temple, the Padawan ascended the steps and built a blue-bladed lightsaber, which unintentionally woke a [[Forge Guardian|sleeping]] [[jurgoran]] in the caves below.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> The enraged creature blocked the path back to the Temple, forcing the young Jedi to kill the jurgoran to safely depart from the Forge.<ref name="Putting Your New Weapon to Use">{{TORcite|type=bonus|Putting Your New Weapon to Use|Tython}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

==Aftermath==
{{GameLSmechanics|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
{{Quote|You arrived on Tython a Padawan, but you leave a Knight of the Republic. May the Force be with you.|Grand Master Satele Shan|<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />}}
The conflict on Tython, while relatively localized, had far-reaching consequences that would help shape the events of the [[Galactic War]] that was to come.<ref name="Acts">{{TORcite|Jedi Knight Storyline, Acts II and III}}</ref> The apprentice of Orgus Din, whom [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Satele Shan believed had more than passed the Trials during the uprising, was granted the rank of Jedi Knight and became a pivotal figure in the conflict with the Sith Empire&mdash;beginning with the Knight's first [[Mission to Coruscant (Desolator crisis)|mission]] on Coruscant. There, the Knight and T7-O1 teamed up with Kira Carsen to stop the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Tarnis (Sith Lord)|Tarnis]] from using the [[Planet Prison]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] against Coruscant.<ref name="Race to the Ruins">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Race to the Ruins|Coruscant}}</ref> Tarnis's [[Duel in the Jedi Temple ruins|death]] at the hands of the Knight sparked the [[Desolator crisis|crisis]] surrounding the [[Desolator (superweapon)|Desolator]] superweapon, during which Tarnis's father [[Darth Angral]] attempted to destroy the Republic and the Jedi Order using stolen Republic superweapons.<ref name="Act I">{{TORcite|Jedi Knight Act I Storyline}}</ref> The Knight returned to Tython at the end of the crisis, [[Battle of the Oppressor|dueling and defeating]] the Sith [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] aboard the latter's [[Starship/Legends|ship]], the [[Oppressor (Harrower-class)|''Oppressor'']], to stop Angral from devastating the planet with the Desolator weapon.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Fate of the Jedi|the ''Oppressor''}}</ref>

[[File:Uphrades.png|thumb|left|200px|After testing the superweapon on the agriworld of [[Uphrades]], Angral planned to use the Desolator on Tython.]]
The conflict also had a powerful influence on Bengel Morr, as the [[Jedi healer/Legends|Jedi healers]] of the Temple were able to heal the Nautolan of his insanity. He remained on Tython for quite some time, retraining in the ways of the Jedi and learning to come to terms with his actions during the uprising.<ref name="Message 1">{{TORcite|Ship Holorecording 1 from Bengel Morr}}</ref> Morr remained in contact with Din's former apprentice throughout his time on Tython, thanking the Jedi for saving him and expressing regret at the loss of Din during the Knight's [[Mission to Alderaan (Desolator crisis)|mission]] to Alderaan.<ref name="Message 2">{{TORcite|Ship Holorecording 2 from Bengel Morr}}</ref> Morr later served on the [[Battle of Corellia|battlefields]] of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] during the next war, where he fought as a full Jedi Knight under the command of the Knight&mdash;known as the "Hero of Tython" by that point&mdash;when Grand Master Shan appointed the Hero the [[Supreme Commander]] of all Jedi forces.<ref name="Jedi Commander">{{TORcite|type=class|Jedi Knight|Jedi Commander|Corellia}}</ref>

With the loss of their leaders Morr<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> and Keshk, who died sometime during the conflict,<ref name="Option">[[Keshk]], as a default environmental character, can be [[Death/Legends|killed]] by both [[Jedi Consular|Consulars]] and [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Knights]], so this article assumes that the [[Flesh Raider]] met his end one way or another.</ref> the organization of the Flesh Raider army dissolved. Without Morr's influence, the natives returned to their normal pattern of occasional raids and in-fighting. Also as a result of the conflict, the Jedi Order began to actively aid and cooperate with the villagers of Kalikori<ref name="Tao'Ven Message">{{TORcite|Email from Ranna Tao'Ven}}</ref> on the advice of Din and his student. Matriarch Tao'Ven turned herself over to the Council for judgment, but they allowed her to remain in her position as a way of allowing her to atone for her actions.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> She later sent a message to the Knight, apologizing for her role in the betrayal, and informing the Jedi how the newfound alliance between the Order and Kalikori was benefiting both parties and had eliminated the dangers of living on Tython.<ref name="Tao'Ven Message" />
{{Endgame}}

==Notable participants==
{{GameLSmechanics|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
===Jedi Order===
====Orgus Din====
[[File:Orgus_Din.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|Orgus Din}}
A well-respected Jedi Master and member of the Jedi Council, Orgus Din was a veteran of the Great Galactic War and the Sacking of Coruscant. During the Sacking, Din personally fought the Sith Lord [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Angral,<ref name="ToP:ToC">''[[The Old Republic, Threat of Peace Act 1: Treaty of Coruscant]]''</ref> sparking a rivalry that would extend to both men's apprentices.<ref name="Race to the Ruins" /> When Din's apprentice Bengel Morr was lost in the destruction of the Jedi Temple, he refused to take on another until witnessing a young initiate's defeat of the Dark Jedi Callef in the Tythonian Gnarls.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" /> Following what he believed was the will of the Force, Din took on the apprentice as his Padawan, and the two began to investigate the recent activities of the native Flesh Raiders.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> During the course of the uprising, he learned that Morr was behind the attack<ref name="Enemy Force" /> and participated in several raids on the Flesh Raider command base and other scattered camps across the planet.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /><ref name="Dark Temptations" /> Thanks to the Pilgrims of Kalikori Village, Din was captured by Morr and taken to the Forge, but Din's new apprentice followed and was able to defeat the Dark Jedi. As a result of the Padawan's actions, Din instructed his student to construct a lightsaber, and upon returning to the Temple he and Grand Master Satele Shan elevated the apprentice to the rank of Jedi Knight.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

====Orgus Din's apprentice====
{{Main|Hero of Tython}}
A young Jedi initiate with remarkable martial skills and combat experience, the apprentice was trained under several Masters before being sent to Tython to face the Jedi Trials. The initiate's arrival was disrupted by the Flesh Raider invasion of the Tythonian Gnarls, and the young Jedi helped stop the attack by single-handedly defeating the Dark Jedi Callef.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" /> Taken on by Master Orgus Din as a Padawan, the apprentice was sent on several missions on behalf of both the Jedi Order and the Pilgrims of Kalikori Village during the uprising, all the while learning more about the natives' motives.<ref name="Enemy Force" /><ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /><ref name="High-Tech Savages" /><ref name="Dark Temptations" /> During the course of the conflict, Din learned that his former apprentice Morr was leading the Flesh Raiders against the Jedi,<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> and the Jedi Master was eventually captured when the Pilgrims betrayed him to Morr.<ref name="Dark Temptations" /> Joining forces with T7-O1,<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> the astromech droid whom the apprentice had rescued on an earlier mission,<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> the Padawan followed Morr to the ancient machine known as the Forge and rescued Din, defeating the Dark Jedi in a duel. As a result of the apprentice's actions during the uprising, Din and Grand Master Satele Shan elevated the Padawan to Jedi Knight and sent the Jedi to Coruscant to investigate a dark presence there&mdash;a darkness that was later revealed to be the Sith Lord Tarnis.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

====T7-O1====
[[File:T7-O1.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|T7-O1}}
An astromech droid with a long history of adventures,<ref name="T7 Convo">{{TORcite|Conversations with T7-O1}}</ref> T7-O1 served the Jedi Order as a reconnaissance droid<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> after his previous partner, Jedi Master [[Ven Zallow]], fell in combat with the Sith Lord [[Darth Malgus]] during the fall of the Jedi Temple.<ref name="Deceived">{{TORweb|url=info/media/trailers/deceived-cinematic-trailer|text=Deceived Cinematic Trailer|int=Deceived}}</ref> A quirky and intelligent droid, T7-O1 was very loyal to his masters<ref name="T7 Comments">{{TORcite|Various comments made by T7-O1 throughout later quests affirm his remarkable loyalty to and confidence in his partners, such as his belief that he and the Hero are unstoppable together.}}</ref>&mdash;whom he referred to as "partners"<ref name="T7 Convo" />&mdash;and was confident that he and his companions could overcome any obstacle.<ref name="T7 Comments" /> In the early [[Standard day/Legends|days]] of the uprising, T7-O1 was captured on a reconnaissance mission by the Flesh Raiders, who stored him in a weapons cache in the Tythos Ridge. There, he witnessed Bengel Morr giving orders to Callef and the Flesh Raiders, and he immediately displayed this recording to Orgus Din upon being rescued by Din's apprentice.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> T7-O1 later joined the Padawan on a rescue mission when Din was captured by Morr and the Flesh Raiders, and with the droid's help the apprentice successfully defeated the Dark Jedi and his servants at the Forge.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> T7-O1 continued to travel with the Jedi,<ref name="The Jedi Envoy" /> who was elevated to the rank of Jedi Knight,<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> on missions across the galaxy during the conflict with Darth Angral and beyond.<ref name="Acts" />

===Pilgrims===
====Ranna Tao'Ven====
[[File:Ranna.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|Ranna Tao'Ven}}
The daughter of Matriarch Sumari, Ranna Tao'Ven came to Tython as a child with her mother and the rest of the Pilgrims. When her mother became deathly ill, Tao'Ven began to take over her duties as Matriarch,<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> and succeeded Sumari as leader when she died of her illness during the uprising.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> Despite her mother's anger at the Jedi for abandoning the Pilgrims to the Flesh Raiders, Tao'Ven grew close to the young apprentice of Orgus Din during the conflict after the Jedi helped recover weapons for the villagers<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> and saved the Twi'leks' crop fields from sabotage.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> When Bengel Morr approached the villagers behind her back with an offer of peace in exchange for Din, Tao'Ven only agreed to the deal if Din's apprentice would not be harmed. When the villagers attempted to kill the young Jedi to satisfy Morr's new terms, she protected the apprentice with her own life and begged for forgiveness. In an attempt to redeem herself, Tao'Ven gave the apprentice information on Morr's location and presented herself to the Jedi Council for judgment.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

====Moorint====
[[File:Moorint.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|Moorint}}
The Scout Chief of Kalikori Village during the uprising, Moorint used the information gathered by his scouts to aid Orgus Din and his apprentice in the fight against the Flesh Raiders.<ref name="Enemy Force" /><ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> A pragmatic and serious man, Moorint was well-versed in combat thanks to his experience fighting the Flesh Raiders, and he believed that thinning the ranks of the enemy and removing their technological advantages was more important than adding to the village's defenses.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> However, Moorint cared deeply for his village, and he was willing to do anything to save his fellow colonists&mdash;even if it meant sacrificing Din to Bengel Morr and killing the young Jedi who helped the villagers defend themselves. When Moorint and several other villagers attempted to kill Din's apprentice to satisfy the Dark Jedi's terms, the apprentice was able to use the Force to convince them to leave peacefully without harming them.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" />

===Flesh Raiders===
====Bengel Morr====
[[File:Bengel_Morr.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|Bengel Morr}}
The apprentice of Orgus Din during the Great Galactic War, Bengel Morr was present during the attack on the Jedi Temple and barely survived. Going into hiding, he went insane and turned against the Jedi Order, believing that it was too weak to destroy the Sith.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> Morr became a Dark Jedi, taking on the Human Callef as his apprentice, and the two began to marshal the native Flesh Raiders of Tython into an army.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> Intending to burn the Jedi Order to the ground and rebuild it into something stronger,<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> Morr began to train Force-sensitive Flesh Raiders as Force Adepts,<ref name="Enemy Force" /> and he targeted his former Master Orgus Din when the latter took on a new apprentice. Making a deal with Kalikori Village, Morr traded protection for the life of Din, and took the captive Jedi Master to the Forge. However, Din's apprentice escaped from Morr's trap and pursued the Dark Jedi, dueling him before the ancient machine and successfully defeating him.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> The Nautolan was healed of his insanity by Jedi healers,<ref name="Message 1" /> and he completed his training<ref name="Message 2" /><ref name="Message 3">{{TORcite|Ship Holorecording 3 from Bengel Morr}}</ref> and served as a Jedi Knight under the apprentice&mdash;who became renowned as a Jedi Knight known as the Hero of Tython&mdash;on the battlefields of Corellia.<ref name="Jedi Commander" />

====Callef====
[[File:Callef.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|Callef}}
Callef was the Human apprentice of Bengel Morr. Arrogant and cruel, Callef was trained as a Dark Jedi by Morr in the decade following the Treaty of Coruscant.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> When Morr prepared to launch his attack upon the Jedi Order, he tasked Callef with leading an invasion force against the Jedi outpost in the region known as the Tythonian Gnarls. However, Callef overestimated his abilities, and fell in combat with a young apprentice sent to stop the Flesh Raiders from entering the Gnarls.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" />

====Keshk====
[[File:Keshk.png|right|100px]]
{{Main|Keshk}}
A hulking Flesh Raider who stood twice as tall as a normal Human and wielded a massive bladed weapon, Keshk assumed the role of Grand Chieftain among his people at some point before the uprising. He served Morr as leader of the Flesh Raider army. He was marshaling his forces in the ruins of the ancient city<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> when he and his bodyguards were killed by a Jedi.<ref name="Option" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The conflict with the Flesh Raiders appears in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'',<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" /> a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] released by [[BioWare]] and [[LucasArts]] on [[December 20]], [[2011]].<ref name="TORRelease">{{TORweb|url=info/news/news-article/20111014-1|text=Global Launch for The Old Republic}}</ref> The uprising represents the [[in-universe]] events of the Jedi Knight class storyline during the first half of the Prelude, when the player arrives on Tython and is forced to defend the Jedi outpost in the Gnarls from Flesh Raider attacks. The class storyline consists of six missions overall, with multiple objectives within each mission and several bonus missions.<ref name="Attack of the Flesh Raiders" /><ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /><ref name="Enemy Force" /><ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /><ref name="High-Tech Savages" /><ref name="Dark Temptations" /> The six missions can be split into a total of seven individual events, with the mission "The Face of the Enemy" consisting of a raid on a shield generator and a fight in Kalikori's crop fields.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" />

As the exact timeframe of ''The Old Republic'' is uncertain, the chronology of many of the class storylines is not precisely known.<ref name="Time" /> However, several statements made during the course of the game indicate that the [[Jedi Consular|Consular]] storyline on Tython occurs before the Jedi Knight storyline. Jedi Master Bela Kiwiiks is not present during the Consular storyline, as she and Kira Carsen are on a mission off-world until early in the Jedi Knight storyline.<ref name="High-Tech Savages" /> Ranna Tao'Ven is also referred to as the Matriarch's daughter throughout the Consular's storyline,<ref name="Pilgrims" /> since she only becomes Matriarch when her mother Sumari dies during the Jedi Knight class storyline. Therefore, the Consular storyline must precede the Jedi Knight's storyline, and the Consular missions are not considered part of the uprising.<ref name="The Face of the Enemy" /> The optional world missions, which are available to both classes, are assumed to precede the Knight's storyline because the Flesh Raider army dissolves after the battle with Bengel Morr, and Kalikori forms an alliance with the Order against the Flesh Raiders.<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> As the side missions are available to both Jedi Knight and Consular players,<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> the identities of the individuals who completed the side missions are unclear due to game mechanics.

[[File:HeroSaber.png|thumb|left|200px|Dark side players who release Morr receive a green crystal instead of this standard blue crystal.]]
As the Jedi Knight is a Republic character, this article assumes that only light side options are chosen, and that the optional game mechanics aspects of the story are completed. The [[canon]]ical species, [[Gender/Legends|gender]], and names of the eight player characters are unknown, so this article also refrains from mentioning anything about the Knight's identity or gender. Several missions present alignment options that may result in slightly different events during the course of the Prelude, but the overall storyline remains the same. The major alignment choice in the Prelude appears in the final mission, "Weapon of the Jedi." Sparing Bengel Morr, whether by allowing him to leave or knocking him unconscious,<ref name="Weapon of the Jedi" /> results in the player encountering him on Corellia during Act III. If the player chooses the dark side option of letting him leave, he or she is forced to fight Morr again and potentially kill him, while knocking him out results in his redemption and assignment to Corellia under the Knight's command.<ref name="Jedi Commander" />
